_note: Model/price catalog — THE single source of truth for the whole project. USD per 1M tokens. Every price/limit the code uses comes from here; add or update models/providers HERE, never in code. Fields per model: `input`, `output` (normal token prices); `cache_read` (price of a cache HIT), `cache_write` (price to CREATE the cache entry); `cache_min` (smallest stable prefix the provider will cache, tokens). Per provider: `cache_mode` = 'explicit' (caching is opt-in — Anthropic cache_control; 'enable caching' is a real fix we prove with a live write->read round-trip) or 'auto' (provider caches eligible prefixes automatically — OpenAI always-on, Google implicit on 2.5+; 'enable' is a no-op, but a per-call prefix that BREAKS the stable region still defeats the auto-cache, so restructuring still applies). NOTE ON READ/WRITE: there is NO separate read/write price for NORMAL tokens — that is just input/output. 'read/write' exists only for CACHING (read = cache hit, write = cache creation). Verified Aug 2026: Anthropic cache read 0.1x / write 1.25x (5-min; 1-hr write is 2x); OpenAI GPT-5.6 cache read 0.1x / write 1.25x; Google implicit read 0.1x, no per-token write fee but explicit caching adds storage $1-4.50/1M/hr. Sources: platform.claude.com/docs pricing, developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing. Anthropic base prices verified (Opus 4.8 5/25, Sonnet 3/15, Haiku 4.5 1/5). OpenAI GPT-5.6 base updated to the Jul-2026 family (Sol 5/30, Terra 2/12, Luna 0.20/1.20). Google base spot-checked; VERIFY any specific SKU against the live pricing page before trusting its $ (third-party sources disagree on some tiers). haiku-4-5 cache_min is 4096 (MEASURED: a 3362-tok prefix did not cache, 7002 did). Per model also: `tier` = capability class (frontier > balanced > small > nano) and `release` = approximate launch (YYYY-MM, verify). The DOWNGRADE ladder now uses `tier`, NOT file order: util.next_cheaper steps ONE tier down to the most-capable callable model there (the gentlest drop) — so a newer cheap 'flash' is never mistaken for a downgrade target of an older pricier 'pro'. File order is therefore cosmetic (kept price-descending for reading). `release` dates are approximate — verify against the provider before quoting recency. Unknown models fall back to a default price in code.
_alias_note: Aliases map a legacy/dated/variant id onto a catalog entry that is the SAME model at the SAME price and tier (a dated snapshot, a '-latest' pointer, or a minor patch). NEVER alias across generations or capability tiers — that would misreport the model and feed the wrong tier into the downgrade ladder; give such a model its own entry instead.
